subject: Next steps: BrightPath integration pilot & local SDK smoke plan
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Walsh <erin@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-25T15:08:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap: BrightPath integration discovery — SDK & local pilot

Hi Erin — thanks again for a great call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a short pilot standing up next week.

Recap (what we heard)
- Goal: Add a conversational assistant into BrightPath Care Portal for triage and quick chart search. Low-latency replies + safe, auditable outputs, and an embeddings-based semantic search over internal docs.
- Requirements: Private data handling (REQ-legal), SSO for internal users, embedding index for clinical docs, reranking for relevance, and structured tool outputs for actions (create note / suggest CPT).

Proposed technical focus areas (pilot scope)
1) SDK quickstart (Python + TypeScript): clone sample app, run locally, exercise text generation + embeddings + tool calling.
2) Auth: prototype using API keys for pilot (short-lived keys) + prepare OIDC flow for Dedicated/Private later.
3) Routing & model selection: start with a small LLM variant for convo path and a cheaper embedding model for semantic search; routing policy for fallback to a lower-cost model on heavy load.
4) Structured output / tool calling: wire a simple "create-incident" tool (JSON schema) and validate outputs against a strict schema before sending to BrightPath APIs.
5) Embeddings + reranker: index a subset of clinical FAQ and run a reranker over top-K to boost precision.

Immediate ask / next steps
- Erin: confirm a 1-hour pilot kickoff window next week (Mon/Tue preferred) and point us to a short list of sample docs (PDFs or Markdown).
- BrightPath: share a low-privilege service account or temporary S3/Share link for the doc subset.
- Karthik / Mateo: prepare local quickstart bundle (Python/TS) and a Docker dev container for BrightPath to run with minimal deps.

Deliverables by EOD Friday (internal owner)
- Mateo: SDK quickstart README + example Python and TS snippets.
- Karthik: sample Dockerfile and routing policy template.
- Lauren: coordinate legal note re: data handling required for pilot.

Attachments: I’ll attach a condensed README and a one-sheet action plan.

Thanks — excited to get hands on.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.ai

From: Erin Walsh <erin@brightpath.ai>

Date: 2026-11-26T09:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: BrightPath integration discovery — SDK & local pilot

Thanks Mateo — this is very clear and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:
- Pilot data: we can provide a redacted set of 150 clinical FAQ items and 30 sample visit notes. Would that be sufficient for an initial embedding + rerank test?
- Compliance: our security org prefers OIDC when possible but okay to start with time-limited API keys for the pilot if we get a clear rotation window.
- Users: the primary pilot audience will be two product engineers and a clinical SME; they will run local tests.

Availability: I can do a kickoff on Monday 2026-11-29 10:00-11:00 PST or Tuesday 2026-11-30 14:00-15:00 PST. Which works best for your team?

Also attaching a short note on data redaction approach (see attachment stub: brightpath-redaction-guidelines.pdf).

— Erin
Erin Walsh
Head of Product, BrightPath Health
erin@brightpath.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>, Erin Walsh <erin@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-26T12:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: BrightPath integration discovery — SDK & local pilot

Thanks Erin — 150 FAQ + 30 notes is a good starting corpus for pilot-level embedding experiments. A few technical notes and suggested commands so the BrightPath engineers can run locally without friction:

Local SDK quickstart (high level)
- Repo: https://drive.google.com/sample-repo-redwood-sdk (we'll invite you directly)
- Python: virtualenv -> pip install redwood-sdk; run examples/generate.py and examples/embeddings_index.py
- TypeScript: npm install @redwood/inference; run ts-samples/chat.ts and ts-samples/embeddings.ts
- Docker dev container: Dockerfile + docker-compose.yml that mounts your sample docs and exposes a local HTTP shim to demo tool calling. We will include a small SQLite index for the embeddings vector store.

Auth options for pilot
- Fast path: short-lived API key (rotate every 24 hours) — simplest for first 48 hours.
- Config path: OIDC setup for Dedicated/Private — we’ll prepare a spec doc and the IDP redirect URIs you’ll need.

Structured output / tool calling
- We'll provide a JSON schema for the create-incident tool. The SDK quickstart includes a validator step (JSON schema validation) before the tool call is executed.

Network / infra asks
- If you have an internal dev box behind firewall, please share an IP allowlist for outbound to redwood endpoints or we can run everything locally against the dev container.

I’ll drop a minimalist Dockerfile and a routing policy example to the sharedDrive and attach here.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: BrightPath integration discovery — SDK & local pilot

Attaching the initial quickstart bundle and the pilot action plan (attachment stubs included below). Links and short instructions are in the README.

Attachment stubs:
- redwood-sdk-quickstart-README.md (contains pip/npm install, env vars, sample run commands, schema validator steps)
- brightpath-pilot-action-plan.xlsx (owner matrix, target metrics, timeline)

Quick run notes for BrightPath engineers
1) Clone sample-repo and open examples/generate.py (Python) or ts-samples/chat.ts (TS).
2) Create a local .env with REDWOOD_API_KEY=<<temp-key>> and REDWOOD_ENV=dev.
3) Start docker-compose: docker compose up --build (this brings up local shim and sqlite index).
4) Run examples/embeddings_index.py to index sample docs; run examples/rerank_demo.py to see reranker hits.

If the BrightPath team wants, Karthik and I can do a short pairing session during the kickoff to get the local container up.

— Mateo

All good — Monday 11/29 at 10:00 PST works for us, please send the calendar invite. We reviewed the README and the action plan; the BrightPath engineers will pull the sample repo tonight and try the Docker flow.

One quick ask before kickoff: can you include a checklist item for token rotation steps and a short blurb about what logs/audit trails Redwood exposes in the dev flow? Our security lead will want that covered in the first 30 minutes of the kickoff.

Thanks — looking forward to the session.

— Erin
